M Khaled Ahmed, Advocate—For the Review Petitioner.

parties:
Mainul Alam ------ Petitioner
vs
Anjera Begum ------ Opposite Party
full_judgment:
Mashuque Hossain Ahmed J: This Review Petition has been preferred by defendant opposite-party No. 10 of Civil Miscellaneous Case No. 37 of 2006 filed under section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure for transferring Title Suit No. 142 of 2000 from the Court of the Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar Bhola, to any other district on the ground stated in the petition. Subsequently, another petition was filed for transferring Title Suit No. 83 of 2005 from that Court to any other district for holding simultaneous trial with Title Suit No. 142 of 2000. This Court by the impugned judgment and order, dated 6-8-2007, allowed the miscellaneous case and transferred both the aforesaid title suits to the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Barisal, for disposal. 

 2. On behalf of the review-petitioner, the learned Advocate Mr M Khaled Ahmed submitted that he missed the list due to the illness of his clerk and could not be present at the time of hearing of the Miscellaneous case. He further submitted that had he been present, he could place his submissions on behalf of the opposite party and if his points were considered, then the face of the Miscellaneous case would have been otherwise. He submitted that the observation of this Court that the petitioner of Miscellaneous Case No. 37 of 2006 (plaintiff of Title Suit No. 142 of 2000) is a resident of another place is erroneous. To that effect, he drew our attention to the address of the petitioner and claimed that she is a permanent resident of Bhola. So, she is not to face the hazardous journey to go to Bhola. Further, he submitted that Title Suit No. 83 of 2005 has been transferred without issuing any Rule. So, this petitioner had no scope to file any objection against that petition. He submitted that the grounds stated in the petition filed under section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure did not exist when the petition was heard. To that effect, he submitted that at that time there were neither political influence nor the Presiding Officer of that Court was present and that the allegation of lingering the hearing of the suit does not stand. So, he submitted that the impugned judgment and order is liable to be reviewed. 

 3. On behalf of the opposite-party (petitioner in Civil Miscellaneous Case No. 37 of 2006) the learned Advocate Mr Tapan Kumar Chakraborty submitted that there was political influence at that time for which the learned trial Court felt embarrassed and lingered the hearing of the suit for days together. He submitted that still the review-petitioner has got his influence in the locality. So, the opposite-party apprehends that she will not get fair justice in that Court. 

 4. We have heard the submissions of the learned Advocates of both the parties. It is admitted that the scope to review a judgment is very limited and until and unless it comes within the four corners of the ingredients specified in Order XLVII, rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure, no judgment can be reviewed to correct any mistake or erroneous decision by taking the power of the appellate Court. In that light we are to examine the impugned judgment sought to be reviewed. Firstly, we find that the observation of the Court that the petitioner of Miscellaneous Case No. 37 of 2006 is a resident of another place is erroneous, as from the very petition her permanent address is found to be at Bhola. The second ground of political influence does not stand under the regime of the Caretaker Government. Further, delay to dispose of the suit also does not stand, as the Presiding Officer of the Court concerned has been transferred to another district long before. In the judgment we find apparent mistake in the face of the record that the Court erroneously considered the petitioner to be a resident of another place. Further, the Court transferred Title Suit No. 83 of 2005 without issuing any Rule. This is also a mistake committed by this Court which is apparent from the face of the record. In view of that, we find merit in the review petition. 

 5. Accordingly, the review petition is allowed. The impugned judgment and order, dated 6-8-2007, is reviewed and the Civil Miscellaneous Case No. 37 of 2006 stands dismissed. The Title Suit Nos. 142 of 2000 and 83 of 2005 which were withdrawn from the Court of the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Bhola and were transferred to the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Barisal are withdrawn from the file of Senior Assistant Judge, Barisal and retransferred to the Court of the Senior Assistant Judge, Bhola.
